data.narrative:
The Bot Company is a Series B–stage robotics and manufacturing venture that has raised approximately $550M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of three same-stage, same-sector peers (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) alongside broader market context spanning nine private robotics companies and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $1.0B. The peer-median approach anchors on three direct comparables valued at $1.6B–$2.0B, with a median of $1.8B. These peers represent identical sector and stage positioning and therefore carry substantial weight.

Synthesizing both methods produces a triangulated range of $888M (floor) to $2.0B (ceiling), with a median point of $1.4B. The peer-median result ($1.8B) sits in the upper half of this range and likely represents the more defensible anchor given the direct comparability of the three reference companies. Key uncertainties include the capital efficiency and unit economics of The Bot Company relative to named peers, runway and burn trajectory through Series C, and near-term commercial traction in manufacturing robotics—a sector sensitive to capex cycles and customer concentration risk.
